question: A 24-year-old man presents with a painless genital ulcer for the past 2 weeks. He reports that he recently has been having unprotected sex with multiple partners. Past medical history is unremarkable. On physical examination, a single ulcer is present on the dorsal shaft of the penis which is circumscribed, indurated, and partially healed. There is moderate inguinal lymphadenopathy but no buboes. Which of the following tests would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

options.opa: Viral and rickettsial disease research laboratory (VDRL) test
options.opb: Swab the chancre and perform a saline wet mount
options.ope: Perform a darkfield microscopic examination of a swab from the chancre

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Painless genital ulcer" -> "Unprotected sex with multiple partners" -> "Single ulcer on dorsal shaft of the penis" -> "Circumscribed, indurated, partially healed" -> "Moderate inguinal lymphadenopathy" -> "No buboes" -> "Likely diagnosis of syphilis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Likely diagnosis of syphilis" -> "Confirmatory test needed" -> "Perform a darkfield microscopic examination of a swab from the chancre" -> 95%
analysis: The most likely diagnosis in this patient is syphilis, which presents with a painless genital ulcer (chancre) and inguinal lymphadenopathy. The confirmatory test for syphilis is the fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) test.
